title: Compatible Kummer tower Cech comparisons with fixed rotation coordinates
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $H$ be a commutative ring of characteristic $p$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in H$, with $r\geq0$. For every positive integer $n$ prime to $p$, fix a primitive root $\zeta_n\in H$ with $\zeta_m^{m/n}=\zeta_n$ when $n\mid m$ and with $\zeta_n^a-\zeta_n^b$ a unit for distinct residues $a,b$ modulo $n$. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$, with empty product $1$,
$$U=\operatorname{Spec}H[1/f],\quad X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(H[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i)[1/f],\quad\Gamma_n=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r.$$
Use the divisibility power transitions $X_m\to X_n$ and the reduction transitions $\Gamma_m\to\Gamma_n$. Set $X=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}X_n$ and $G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^r$, where $q$ runs over primes; identify $G=\varprojlim_n\Gamma_n$ by the usual residue coordinates. For an affine scheme $W$ and a profinite set $P$, write $W[P]$ for the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions of $W$ indexed by finite continuous quotients of $P$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].

The rotations $x_i\mapsto\zeta_n^{a_i}x_i$ define compatible actions of $\Gamma_n$ on $X_n$ and of $G$ on $X$. The comparisons
$$\coprod_{g\in\Gamma_n}X_n\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X_n\times_UX_n,\quad(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx),\qquad X[G]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X\times_UX$$
are isomorphisms of schemes. They identify triple vertices $(x,gx,hgx)$ with successive labels $g,h$, so the direct first-to-third label is $hg$. The comparisons commute with all divisibility transitions and with base changes $H\to H'$ that preserve the parameters and compatible roots. For a characteristic-$p$ ring $H'$ carrying parameters $t_i'$ and compatible primitive roots $\zeta_n'$ with the same unit-difference property, and a ring map $H\to H'$ carrying $\zeta_n$ to $\zeta_n'$, they also commute with substitutions $t_i\mapsto u_it_i'$ accompanied by compatible roots $v_{i,n}$ of the units $u_i$, where $v_{i,n}^n=u_i$ and $v_{i,m}^{m/n}=v_{i,n}$ for $n\mid m$, with root-coordinate map $x_{i,n}\mapsto v_{i,n}x_{i,n}'$; both product projections and every rotation coordinate commute with that map. For $r=0$ the comparisons are the identity comparison and $G=1$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, simultaneous root rotations; agent-formulated compatible punctured root-algebra CRT and inverse-limit calculation.

proof.text: First suppose $H$ is the zero ring. Every root algebra and localization is zero, all schemes in the assertion are empty, and the scheme comparisons and diagrams are unique. Otherwise put $A=H[1/f]$ and $B_n=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i$; this is $(H[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i)[1/f]$, the ring of $X_n$, since both have the same maps to any ring: maps from $H$ inverting $f$ together with $n$-th roots of the images of the $t_i$. Each $t_i$ is a unit in $A$, with inverse $(\prod_{j\ne i}t_j)/f$; each $x_i$ is a unit in $B_n$, with inverse $x_i^{n-1}/t_i$. These formulas remain valid when a punctured ring is zero. The set $N_p$ of positive prime-to-$p$ integers is small and directed by divisibility: a common upper bound is the least common multiple.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, simultaneous root presentation and rotations; agent-written coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Write $H_n=H[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i$ and $H_\infty=\varinjlim_{n\in N_p}H_n$. A compatible family $H_n[1/f]\to C$ is exactly a compatible family $H_n\to C$ whose common image of $f$ is invertible. By the colimit and localization universal properties it is exactly a map $H_\infty[1/f]\to C$. Thus $B=\varinjlim_n B_n=H_\infty[1/f]$. The small-colimit spectrum lemma identifies $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the specified scheme inverse limit.

For $a\in\Gamma_n$, evaluation $x_i\mapsto\zeta_n^{a_i}x_i$ preserves $x_i^n=t_i$, is independent of residue representatives, and has inverse given by $-a$. Composition adds the residues. If $n\mid m$, then $(\zeta_m^{a_i}x_{i,m})^{m/n}=\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,m}^{m/n}$, so the power transitions intertwine rotations and residue reduction. Passing to the colimit of rings gives an action on $X$ of the compatible residue families. This is an action on schemes since the equalities are identities on algebra generators.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, simultaneous root presentation and rotations; agent-written coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Fix $n$. A zero coefficient ring gives the unique isomorphism of zero rings; otherwise, over any $B_n$-algebra occurring below, $T^n-1=\prod_{a=0}^{n-1}(T-\zeta_n^a)$. To verify it over rings with zero divisors, divide successively by these monic linear factors. After the first $k$ divisions, evaluation at $\zeta_n^k$ makes the remaining quotient vanish: the other factors evaluate to units. Division is justified by $T^j-c^j=(T-c)\sum_{b=0}^{j-1}T^{j-1-b}c^b$. After $n$ divisions the quotient is $1$, by monicity and degree. The ideals $(T-\zeta_n^a)$ are pairwise coprime, since subtracting their generators gives a unit. Their intersection equals their product: if $I+J=(1)$, write $1=u+v$ with $u\in I,v\in J$, and $z=zu+zv$ for $z\in I\cap J$; induction applies because a product of ideals each coprime to $J$ is coprime to $J$ (multiply elements congruent to $1$ modulo $J$). Consequently the CRT node gives $C[T]/(T^n-1)\cong\prod_{a\bmod n}C$ by evaluations, for each such coefficient ring $C$.

source.place: Tag 00DT, lemma-chinese-remainder; explicit monic division and coprimality calculation for the supplied roots.

proof.text:
The affine fibre-product lemma gives $X_n\times_U X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B_n\otimes_A B_n)$, with the two specified coefficient maps. By polynomial evaluation this tensor algebra is $B_n[y_1,\ldots,y_r]/(y_i^n-t_i)_i$: its maps to any algebra amount to the two compatible $B_n$-maps. Substitute $z_i=y_i/x_i$; the inverse is $y_i=x_i z_i$, so it becomes $B_n[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(z_i^n-1)_i$. Apply step 4 successively to the variables, taking the remaining variables and relations as the coefficient ring at each application. The resulting evaluation isomorphism is
$$B_n\otimes_A B_n\longrightarrow\prod_{a\in\Gamma_n}B_n,\qquad b\otimes c\longmapsto(b\,r_a^*(c))_a.$$
The finite-affine-coproduct lemma turns this into precisely $(x,a)\mapsto(x,ax)$. Its projections are the two displayed tensor inclusions, not merely their maps on geometric points. All calculations allow a zero coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; agent ratio calculation and iterative use of Tag 00DT.

proof.text: Put $L=\varprojlim_{n\in N_p}\mathbf Z/n$, with its subspace topology in the product of finite discrete rings. Given $(z_q)_{q\ne p}$, integer CRT gives the unique $a_n$ with residues $\rho_{v_q(n)}(z_q)$ for $q\mid n$. CRT uniqueness and residue compatibility show $a_m\bmod n=a_n$ for $n\mid m$. Conversely the coordinate ring maps $L\to\mathbf Z/q^b$ are compatible; the adic-residue universal property supplies a unique ring map $L\to\mathbf Z_q$. Residue separation and CRT uniqueness show these constructions are inverse. Each forward coordinate depends on finitely many residues, whose fibres are cosets of $q^b\mathbf Z_q$. Those are open: a sufficiently small norm ball is contained in $q^b\mathbf Z_q$, by the residue node's norm criterion. Conversely equality modulo $q^b$ bounds the norm of the difference by $q^{-b}$, proving continuity of the inverse into each $\mathbf Z_q$. Taking the finite product over the parameters gives $G\cong\varprojlim_n\Gamma_n$ with exactly the stated topological residue coordinates. Here $n=1$ gives the singleton ring.

source.place: Tag 00DT, lemma-chinese-remainder; agent reconstruction using the cited adic-residue universal property (Mathlib realization recorded on that node).

proof.text: Every finite continuous quotient $G\to F$ factors through some $\Gamma_n$. Indeed residue cylinders form a neighbourhood basis by step 6. For each $g$ choose a cylinder about $g$ on which the map is constant; compactness of the profinite set $G$ gives finitely many covering cylinders. A common multiple $n\in N_p$ of their levels refines all of them, so equal residues modulo $n$ give equal values in $F$. The residue map to $\Gamma_n$ is surjective: integer representatives in the finitely many relevant adic factors realize any prescribed residues. Thus the $\Gamma_n$ are a cofinal family of finite quotients. By the test-object definition, $X[G]=\varprojlim_n\coprod_{\Gamma_n}X$. At a fixed finite label set $F$, the finite-coproduct spectrum lemma and step 2 identify $\varprojlim_m\coprod_F X_m=\coprod_F X$: the ring identity $\varinjlim_m\prod_F B_m=\prod_F B$ follows from the elementwise filtered-colimit node applied to $(B_m)_m$: the canonical map is surjective by choosing one common stage for finitely many entries, and injective by choosing one later common stage for finitely many equalities. These arguments include $F$ a singleton.

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; agent finite-cylinder and finite-product universal-property arguments.

proof.text: The finite comparisons commute with transitions: on the component $a\in\Gamma_m$ the map to level $n\mid m$ sends $x_{i,m}$ to $x_{i,m}^{m/n}$ and its rotated value to $\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,m}^{m/n}$, by step 3. Consider $D_{m,n}=\coprod_{\Gamma_n}X_m$. Its diagonal inverse limit equals its double inverse limit: to get the projection to $(m,n)$ from a diagonal cone, choose a common multiple $k$ of $m,n$, and project from $D_{k,k}$; independence of $k$ follows after a further common multiple. Conversely restrict any double cone to the diagonal. Step 7 therefore identifies $\varprojlim_n D_{n,n}=X[G]$. Also $\varprojlim_n(X_n\times_U X_n)=X\times_U X$: a cone is precisely two compatible cones to $X_n$ with the same composite to $U$, by the fibre-product universal property. The inverses of the compatible finite isomorphisms are compatible as well; the two induced limit morphisms are inverse since all projections of their composites are identities. This gives the actual scheme comparison $X[G]\cong X\times_U X$ with first projection $x$ and second projection $gx$. The compatible rotations of step 3 define a scheme action of $G$: apply the same limits to the finite actions; identity and multiplication hold after every projection.

source.place: Tag 01YW and the explicit inverse-limit universal properties; agent diagonal-cone argument.

proof.text: The triple convention follows from the action of steps 3 and 8, without choosing new coordinates. Work on any scheme of test points, allowing labels to vary on its finite open-and-closed pieces. Successive vertices are $x$, $gx$, $h(gx)$; the action identity gives $h(gx)=(hg)x$. At level $n$ the root coordinate on the third vertex is $\zeta_n^{b_i}\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,n}=\zeta_n^{b_i+a_i}x_{i,n}$, so its label relative to the first vertex is $hg$. In the profinite parameter object this identity holds after every finite quotient projection, hence holds in the defining inverse limit. Both projections are the stated vertices by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. This proves the convention as an identity of scheme morphisms, rather than only on geometric points. The triple map $X[G\times G]\to X\times_UX\times_UX$, $(x,g,h)\mapsto(x,gx,hgx)$, is an isomorphism: write $X\times_UX\times_UX=(X\times_UX)\times_{\mathrm{pr}_2,X,\mathrm{pr}_1}(X\times_UX)$ and pull back the double comparison of step 8 on both factors, giving $X[G]\times_{X}X[G]$, formed with $(x,g)\mapsto gx$ on the left and the first projection on the right. By [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], $X[S]=\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$, so this fibre product is $X[G]\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}LC(G,\mathbf Z)=X[G\times G]$, since $LC(G,\mathbf Z)\otimes LC(G,\mathbf Z)=LC(G\times G,\mathbf Z)$ (the quotients $\Gamma_n\times\Gamma_n$ are cofinal among finite quotients of $G\times G$, by the cylinder argument of step 7). Under these identifications the point $(x,g,h)$ has vertices $x,gx,h(gx)$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, explicit simultaneous root presentation; agent coordinate calculation supplement.

proof.text: For the remaining substitution, write $\phi:H\to H'$ with $\phi(t_i)=u_it'_i$ and $\phi(\zeta_n)=\zeta'_n$. Evaluation $x_{i,n}\mapsto v_{i,n}x'_{i,n}$ respects the relations because $(v_{i,n}x'_{i,n})^n=u_it'_i$. It extends to the punctured algebra since $\phi(f)=(\prod_i u_i)\prod_i t'_i$ is invertible there. For $n\mid m$, the two images of $x_{i,n}$ are equal because $(v_{i,m}x'_{i,m})^{m/n}=v_{i,n}(x'_{i,m})^{m/n}$. For every rotation label $a$, the two images of a generator are $\phi(\zeta_n^{a_i})v_{i,n}x'_{i,n}=v_{i,n}(\zeta'_n)^{a_i}x'_{i,n}$. They agree on coefficients as well, proving equality of the algebra maps. Thus the induced scheme map $F_n:X'_n\to X_n$ satisfies $F_n(a x')=aF_n(x')$. The comparison square commutes since its two projections are $F_n(x')$ and $F_n(a x')=aF_n(x')$, while the label stays $a$. Passing to the inverse limits gives the same equalities for $F:X'\to X$ and every finite rotation coordinate. Equality is detected by the limit projections, so this proves the whole profinite square, both product projections and all rotation coordinates. Ordinary base change is the special case $u_i=v_{i,n}=1$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, explicit simultaneous root presentation; agent coordinate calculation supplement.

proof.text: If $r=0$, $f=1$, each $H_n=H$ and every transition is the identity. Thus $X=U=\operatorname{Spec}H$ and $\Gamma_n=G=1$. The map $(x,1)\mapsto(x,x)$ identifies with the identity under $U\times_U U=U$; all substitutions and triple labels reduce to identities.
